name: Vernon Search and Rescue Centre
award: Best Non-Profit Building, Star Building Systems 2025
desc: Ferro partnered with the construction manager and consultant team at the front end of the project to help the Vernon Search and Rescue Society create a space that uses the benefits of a pre-engineered metal building: a functional building with architectural detail and the economies of a pre-engineered structure. Ferro provided design-assist services to help the consultant team realize their and the owner’s vision for the new facility while keeping the structural budget on track. The building incorporates an offset roof slope over the front two-thirds of the building, a mix of alternate cladding to accentuate its structural features, and offset structural elements with storefront glazing. It won Ferro the 2025 Best Non-Profit Building award from Star Building Systems and is featured on Star’s 2026 corporate calendar.

name: Queen Margaret’s Sports Dome
desc: Nestled in the community of Duncan on Vancouver Island, the Queen Margaret’s Sports Dome hosts a world-class gymnasium the school uses for basketball, tennis, volleyball and other fitness activities. Four large skylights bring natural light into the space, and an access building provides changerooms and a common space for students to enter and prepare. A post-and-beam canopy with a metal roof brings wood and steel construction together, and we’re proud of how the facility serves the local community.

name: Saanich West Coast Response Centre
desc: Completed in summer 2021, the WCMRC Saanich facility is an almost exact match to the WCMRC Port Alberni facility. Key features include faux wood-look panels wrapping the east sidewall and north endwall, a canopy over the main entrance, a drive-through covered bay on the south end, and covered exterior stairs to the second-level offices. The facility houses first responders who need to reach spills on BC waters quickly, with all the equipment and materials to contain them and minimize the impact on our environment.

name: Beecher Bay West Coast Response Centre
desc: Built in 2022, the WCMRC facility at Beecher Bay added another spill response centre to WCMRC’s network along BC’s west coast, with maintenance bays and office areas for their operations. Ferro designed and supplied the structure, including post-disaster design, roof safety lifelines, aluminum roof curbs and a steel joist and deck mezzanine, plus a structural steel canopy with membrane roofing over the front entrance and a full composite roof and wall package. Our scope also covered supply and installation of aluminum windows, doors, overhead doors and exterior access stairs to the upper offices, which are clad in wood-patterned aluminum panels.

name: Williams Lake BC Hydro Truck Storage
desc: Built in 2020 on an existing BC Hydro site, this facility gives BC Hydro service vehicles year-round conditioned storage. A full composite roof and wall system provides robust insulation and a clean interior liner, and custom timber canopies over the endwall mandoors are integrated with the wall system for seamless weatherproofing. Clearspan frames give uninterrupted access between four service bays with overhead doors, and the columns and cladding step across two elevations to suit the final site grading.

name: Advance Aerospace Addition
client: Sunjin Aviation c/o Advance Aerospace Inc.
desc: After completing the general contracting work to expand Advance Aerospace’s warehouse at Boundary Bay Airport, Ferro was contracted to install 400 ft of conduit and tie in to the existing pull box on Ottawa Street, coordinating with BC Hydro to bring three-phase power to the expanded facility.

name: Axton Fabrication Expansion
desc: Ferro partnered with Axton Custom Equipment and Manufacturing to expand their existing facility for growth in welding and fabrication. As a design-build project, we took it from initial concept through permit application and preconstruction to a completed facility: a preload before the foundation and slab, an 80′ × 100′ × 30′ pre-engineered building, mechanical and electrical installation, and supply and installation of two 20-ton cranes and six 1-ton jib cranes. The facility was completed in spring 2019.

name: Greenrock Industrial Commercial Centre
desc: Phase 2 of Greenrock Industrial in Nanaimo was built in 2022 with new commercial office and warehouse space. An energy-saver insulation and vapour barrier system on the roof and walls maximizes insulating value, and steel canopies over the overhead doors and main entrance improve weatherproofing. A full aluminum roof curb and structural support beams carry a rooftop unit with a weathertight seal, and the facade alternates horizontal and vertical corrugated cladding as an architectural feature.

name: RJ Industrial Commercial Warehousing
desc: Built in 2014, the RJ Industrial Business Condos provide new commercial office and warehouse space plus a storage building for individual tenants. The main structure uses insulated metal panel wall cladding and a standing seam roof with energy-saver insulation, with full aluminum roof curbs and structural beams carrying rooftop units weathertight. Ferro designed custom architectural buildouts to the front facade with light-gauge framing and insulated metal panels, and the storage building has a mandoor and roll-up door in every bay.

name: Sidney Island Workshop
desc: Just off the southeast coast of Vancouver Island, this workshop of just over 1,000 sq ft houses the owner’s specialty equipment. Ferro worked through the design with the client to give the structure three overhead doors and an offset foundation with a partition wall dividing the interior, and supported the special logistics of barging all materials, insulation included, over to Sidney Island.
